newsitem.title: PERU: Relaxed MRTA rebels played piano as military spied.
newsitem.headline: Relaxed MRTA rebels played piano as military spied.

text.p: Relaxed rebels played the piano, smoked cigarettes and chatted with a visiting aid worker to while away time during their 126-day siege of the Japanese ambassador's home, according to military spy photos published on Monday.

The pictures, apparently taken by minute cameras inserted into periscopes from tunnels dug under the residence, also showed rebels lounging on the floor while they drew slogans on militant banners later placed on the residence's exterior.
One wounded Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebel was also depicted dozing on a carpet with a crutch next to him as he listened to music on a Walkman.

The pictures, published in the local daily La Republica and weekly magazine Si, were a key element in the military's surveillance operation before last Tuesday's attack in which all 14 MRTA rebels were killed and all but one of their 72 hostages freed.
Smiling hostages were shown lying on the floor in shorts and T-shirts playing board games.

MRTA leader Nestor Cerpa was shown sitting back in one of the house's lavish salons, grinning as he talked to fellow guerrillas and International Committee of the Red Cross representative Jean-Pierre Schaerer.
The government expelled Schaerer from Peru about a week before the attack.
The pictures helped the government to discover the daily routines of the MRTA guerrillas and the exact locations of the hostages.
